newsitem.title: UK: Buckingham Palace goes kosher for Weizman visit.
newsitem.headline: Buckingham Palace goes kosher for Weizman visit.

text.p: Pork, meat served with dairy products and shellfish were strictly off the menu when the kitchens of Buckingham Palace went kosher for a banquet for visiting Israeli President Ezer Weizman.

A spokeswoman at Queen Elizabeth's London's residence said on Wednesday that the palace hired one of London's top Jewish caterers, Tony Page, to cook a kosher meal for guests at the sumptuous banquet in Weizman's honour on Tuesday.
"Those people who required a special meal were catered for by an external firm," she said.

The 140 guests at the banquet dined on sole, veal and mango melba. Page and his staff prepared a meal for 30 guests according to strict Jewish dietary law and even provided waiters to serve the Orthodox guests.
Buckingham Palace chefs are accustomed to catering for specific dietary requirements but the spokeswoman said it was rare for quite so many at the same time.

Page, who was not available for comment, is cooking other meals for Weizman during his official three-day state visit to Britain, the first by an Israeli president since the Jewish state was formed from British-occupied Palestine 49 years ago.
